n. Pied Wagtail (bird) (from: -shela).
n. Wagtail (of the Grass Warbler species) (from: -shela).
n. small, narrow piece of land syn. musho- londondo.
n. small shal-low pond syn. sisholwa-sholwa.
n. the pointed piece of wood which projects above the apex of a hut and usually crowned with a pinnacle of plaited grass called 'mutumbwe'.
n. small creature: Kakomu ka kashukuma, small but fully grown cattle. fig. small woman.
v.t. (1) to have ability or skill (in reference to work) (2) to overcome someone der. nashu. cf. -kona. rel. -kashulela (kashulezi) to overcome someone on another's behalf.
n. small fish-hook (from: shuta).
n. rudeness, con-tempt Ku bulela cwalo ki kashwau, it is rude to speak like that. (from -shwaula. syn. Iishwau
n. healthy constitution Ki wa kashwe, he is exceptionally sound in body syn. kanjwe.
n. unpleasant body odour
n. hare, rabbit. fig. a clever cheat, an artful person who misleads others. syn. sanasulwe, shakame, sanondo.
n. grudge against someone, lasting ill-will, hatred often due to one's plans being th-warted, everlasting hatred: Ku yema mutu kasumatondo, to hate somebody
n. a kind of black ant (the sting of which produces a swelling).
n. tuft of hair left on a shaved head. syn. sisumpila, njombi.

v.t. to dig up roots (cassava roots, sweet-potatoes, etc...) der. mukati, sikatiso, muka-telo. rel. -katela (katezi) to dig out for someone. caus. -katisa (kati-size) to order or to help someone to dig. int. -katelela (katelezi) to dig up the lot. ref. -ikatela (ikatezi) to dig up for oneself: Ni sa y'o ika-tela mulyani, I am going to dig up some roots to make medicine

v.t. to strike the ground with a hoe, to make an earthen floor (in a house, etc ) rel. -katela (katezi) to ~ for some-one caus. -katisa (katisize) to order or to help someone to ~ stat. -kateha (katehile) to be even (earthen floor, etc )
interj. with 'kuli', to be laid up continually as an invalid Mukul a sa li kuli kataa! the patient has been laid up for a long time.
n. the upper part of the jaw bone regarded as a vital spot (from -tafuna).
v.i. to hesi-tate, to delay: U sike wa kata- kata, u bulelefela: don't hesitate, speak your mind caus. -katakatisa (kata-katisize) to cause someone to ~.
n. Iouse, chikoe (jigger) syn. nda.
n. African altar made of I sticks on which offerings were made to Nyambe or to ancestors.

v.i. to get tired. ; bored. weary: Lo katezi hahulu, we are very tired. der. mukatala. cf.- -tineha. caus. -katalisa ( katalisize) to overtire, to exhaust in a physi-cal sense: Puka i ni katalisEze. walk-ing in the dew has exhausted me Inv. -katuluha (katuluhile) to rest. caus. -katulusa (katulusize) to give rest ref -ikahlusa (ikatulusize) to take a rest.
n. explorer (lit. somebody who travelled in many countries and saw many things)
n. black spot on the skin of Africans.
vi. to lie down (as an invalid in a long drawn out ill-ness)
n. small fishing mat made of grass.
n. a fairly long dis-tance syn. kahobo.
n. rubbish pit; pit from where plastering earth is dug.
n. kind of protective medicine which, in the past, used So to be taken with the first products of the season (maize, millet, etc. .) (from: -tamuna).
v.t. to meet, to en-counter, to come upon: Ni katani bo muluti mwa nzila, I met the teacher on the way.
v.t. to go out some distance to meet an ex- pected guest. syn. -patoka.
n. the last evacuation of the bowels at the time of death. (from -fa).
n. the apex of a; hut seen from the interior.

n. (1) a ceremonial or traditional act or gesture strictly observed: Ni itumezi kwa lico za mica, kono ni cite, ni ta– watafela ka eza katangu: I thank you for the food, but I have eaten already, I shall just have one or two mouth-fuis to keep the tradition (2) con-straint: Ha ni na katangu ko ni ezize ka ka ta ni tuhelisa mutoho: I did not do any moral wrong or mis-chief which would constrain me from drinking beer.

v.t. to annoy, to trouble, to tire der. mukatazi, katazo, muikatazi, buikatazo. syn. -swenya. rel. -kataleza (katalelize) to offend someone by annoying another: U sike wa ni kataleza mwa-nana, do not annoy my child. stat. -katazeha (katazehile) to be an-noyed, to be troubled fig to be sick: Kacenu ni katazehile hahulu, today I really fecl unwell. rec. -ka-tazana (kahzani or katazanile) to annoy each other. freq. -katazanga to keep on annoying someone. ref. -lkataza (ikatalize) to do one's best. caus. -lkatazisa (ikatazisize) to cause one's own torment: Ku maswe ka ikatazisa musali. bunde ki ka mu leleka fela; it is stupid to worry oneself with home troubles' the best thing is to get a divorce.
n. annoyance, worry, nuisance, bother. (from: -kataza).
n. Eng. church catechism.
v.t. to press down (as meal in a basket, etc)
v.i. to look fine. elegant der. kateleho. syn. -buheha.
n. elegance, beauty, grace. (from: -kateleha).
v.t. to like some-thing, to be pleased with someone or something: Mukwa wa hae ki amunde, na u katelwa: I like his manners, they are pleasant
n. skull, human skull (Rarely applied to animals.)
n. ( l ) gathering of people sitting in a circle; (2) a council of appointed representa-tives mecting once a year cf. Ii- tengo.
n. pipit (bird) gen. n.
n. warbler. Ben.n.
n. maize pounded before being completely soaked.
n. Mbunda. name given to someone who keeps him-self out of troubles (from: -tewa).
v.t. to please, to give pleasure (from -katwa); syn. -tabisa.
n. printing; katiso ya libuka. printing works (from: -hatisa ).
n. braiding (especi-ally on women skirts). (from: -hatisa).
n. engraving on wood made with a red hot-point; (hece, a written letter) (from: -tail) syn. Ii–wati.
n. kind of small ante-lope common in Lupani country. dim. of timba).
n. fontanel. (from: -tofota ).
n. kind of long grass used in making fish traps or as thatch
n. Luyana. small stick or tree dim. of sitondo)
exp. ground left by ancestors. syn. li- tongo).
n. Luyana. small par-ticle of anything which gets in the eye; a mote. fig. complaint: Ha ni na katowati ka mulen'a ka, I have not the least complaint regarding my master
n. woman de-stroying village life by her bad be- haviour (from: -tuba).
v.i. to stand up and go: Lena h'a fumani do ka nwiwa, h'a koni ka katuka kanji; when he finds himself in a place where people are drinking, he has not the will to stand up and go. I
v.t. (bridegroom) to give a sum of money to the girl's parents when taking away his bride from them (This present is given apart from the 'sionda'). der. mukatu. cf. -nanula.
n. judgement, verdict, sentence Taba ye i se I filwe katulo, sentence has already been passed ( from: -atula ).
v.i. to take a rest. (see:-katala)
n. small round basket with lid in which women keep trinkets; (made of 'makenge' roots) cf: lukumbu.
v.i. to canter (horses, cattle) cf.: -kanta. rel. -ka-tuzeza (katuzelize) to ~ towards caus. -katuzisa (katuzisize) to cause to ~

v.t. (1) to value greatly; to enjoy possession of Ni katwa likomu za ka, I value my head of cattle greatly. (2) to be un-willing to give, or part with: Ni katwa kufana kubo ya ka, I am un-willing to give away my blanket rel. -katelwa (katezwi ) (1) to be pleased with, to rejoice in (2) to withhold something from some- one Na ha ni katelwi mute sico, I do not withhold food from anyone. caus. -katisa (katisize) to give pleasure (see -katisa). stat: -kate- leha (katelehike) to be pleasing, fine, elogant
n. trap, snare: Ba teile tutwa mwa masimu. they have set snares in the gardens.
n. person or pack-animal travelling a long time without showing any sign of fa-tigue.
n. Sandmartin (bird).
adv. all, altogether, en-l tirely: kaufel'a bona, all of them. I syn. kamukana.
adv. near, close to; presently, lately: fakaufi ni Mongu, close to Mongu: honafakaufifa, just lately. dim. kauf nyana, very near, very soon. der. bukaufi.

v.i. (1) to become separated. to part with; (2) to divorce: Ngete u kauhani ni musal'a hae, so-and-so has di-vorced his wife der. kauhano, kau-hanyo rel. -kauhanela (kauhanezi) to become separated for some reason or at a certain place caus.- kauhanya (kauhanyize) to cause separation, to disunite, to put asunder int. -kauhanelela (kauha-nelezi) to become separated for good.
n. separation, parting; divorce (from: -kauhana).
n. division; chapter of a book. (from: -kau- hana).
v.i. to be left [ beh ind . syn. siyalela.
v.i. Luyana. to crack, to split der. kauke! syn. -pazuha, -zeuka.
interj. truly! (affirming an oath) (from:-kauka)
v.t. to break. to split, to cut through: Likomu li kauzi mihala, the cattle have cut their ropes rel. kaulela (kaulezi) to ~ for someone. caus. -kaulisa (kauli-size) to cause to ~.
v.t. to contract a ven-ereal disease called 'mukau'.
v.t. to compel someone to leave, against his will, something which he is enjoying (food, beer, etc . )
n. powerful sorcerer (from: -ululula ).
n. shallow fishing pool. syn. sisholwasholwa. kaundwa-undwa, n. twilight, dusk
v.t. to separate people quarrelling or fighting; to appease; to mediate. der. mukaupi.
n. cotton vest with short sleeves; underwear.
n. Button-quail (bird)
v.i. to cease rain-ing: Pula i kaulize, the rain has stopped
n. unpleasant body odour syn. kamwe, kake, mumwe. kasilangandu

v.t. to tie the hind legs of cattle when milking; to tie grass or purlins in building an enclosure der. mukaiso. rel. -kayela (kayezi) to ~ for someone. caus. -kayisa (kayislze) to order or to help someone to ~.
v.t. to mill grain. to grind der. sikayo, mukaiwa. rel. -kayela (kayezi) to ~ for someone. caus. -kayisa (kayisize) to order or to help someone to ~. int. -kaye-lela (kayelezi) to grind the lot
v.t. to make scarifica-tions on a corpse to make sure that the deceased will not leave his death unavenged. der. mukayo.
n. cheat, decciver, liar, crook, twister. syn. mupumi.
v.i. to be in difficulty, in danger, in trouble of any kind. der. Iikayamana. syn. - ziyeleha.
n. temporary shelter made of mats (put up by herdboys and paddiers in open country).
v.t. to give very generously an unexpected gift to someone.
n. Luyana. undue haste in speakmg or doing things. (from: -yeyema )
n. another name for the 'isunde' tree (which mainly grows in old forest gar-dens) (from:-yola)
n. small bin or storing hut, small granary. fig. gizzard of a bird.
n. dance performed by Manyengo men
n. Luyana noun taken adverbially used in the ex- pression: Lu pEla kayoya-nadambo, we subsist because we know how to make the best use of our soil. (from: -yoya).

v.i. to get de-tached or broken (as a branch of a tree) mutai u kayukile kwa kota, a branch broke off the tree. fig. to escape, to get through: Ni kayukile mwa manyando, I have got through the hardship caus. -kayula (kayuzi) to break, to tear off; to set frce. freq. -kayaula (kayauzi) to break in several places. fig. to speak heediessly.
n. person surpas-sing all others (as a great witch, a great hunter, etc ..) (sce: -yunda).
n. kind of leguminous plant common in swamps and which causes severe itching when in contact with human skin. (from: -yuwa).
n. Toka-Leya. weakness, fatigue experienced by some people who cannot go a long way without eating food; dizziness caused by hunger
n. (taken adverbially); quickly: Mu eze kazatu, do it quickly, make haste!
n. scorching sun dim. of lizazi).
n. Eng. domestic cat
n. the first milk of a cow after calving c: mutauluswa.
n. someone making a scarch; spy (from: -zemba).
n. tuft of hair on the ridge-bone of cattle
n. Toka-Leya. Iarge sausage tree (Kigelia Pinnata) syn. mupobta, mapungupungu.
adv. much, very much: Ha ki mutu kwa bumaswe ki ke! what a plain looking person!
may: A mu ke mu hupule pili, may you think first!
ideoph. (sce: ka6)
v.t. to look at someone surreptitiously. rec. -ke- culana (keculani) to look at each other surreptitiously.
v.t. Luyana. to over-look ;to leave without care. der. Iikeela.
v.i. Eng. to cackle (a laying hen).

v.t. to plough. der. mukekeli, mukekelisi, sikekele, mu-kekelelo. rel. -kekelela (kekelezi) to ~ for someone caus. -kekelisa (kekelisize) to order or to help someone to ~. int. -kekelelela (ke-kelelezi) to plough the whole garden ref. -lkekelela (ikekelezi) to plough one's own garden.
v.t. to bite syn. -luma.

v.t. (1) to cut bush or trces all over a place: Ba keketile macacani kaufelafa mabita, they have cleared the bush over the graves syn. -lema. (2) to cause pain all over the body by ill- made scarifications caus. -keketisa (ke-ketisize) to order or to help some-one to cut bush
v.i. to laugh merrily (as children) to giggle
n. a large, beauti-ful animal (ox, etc .): Mulena u lurle namani a kekete tuna ya pulu, the Litunga has presented us with a large, beautiful ox.
n. increment, increase, supplement Ni kafumana lili kekezo kwa mali a ka? when shall I get an increment in my salary? (From: -ekeza).
v.i. to pass by, on the other side, to avoid meeting someone caus. -kekulu-hisa (kekuluhisize) to cause to ~
n. Afrik. church (build-ing or congregation; also applied to school buildings)
v.i. to flow gently or in a small rill as a stream near its source fig. to weep
v.t. to draw or carry water continuously (as when pre-paring beer) int. of -ka).
v.i. to look very old, to look worn out by the infirmities of old age (people or cattle) Musali muXulu yo s'a kele-pani bakenisa matuku. this old woman looks very feeble owing to many illnesses.
n. gland; swelling of a gland in the armpit and groin
n. mutual advice. (from: -eleza).
n. advice, counsel: Ku kupa kelezo, to consult idiom. exp: Kelezo ki mulyani ha i nyefulwi, good advice is a remedy not to be despised

v.i. (1) to turn away, to leave the path: Mu sike mwa keluha mwa nzila, mu ka lateXa: don't leave the path, for you may get lost (2) to act wrongly, to aberrate: ku keluha mwa niti, to deviate from truth. (3) to menstruate der. mekeluhisi, mu- kelusi. syn. -fapuha, -yabuka. rel. -keluhela (keluhezl) to leave the path at (a place), to deviate to-wards, to branch off:fo u Keluhela mukwakwa, where the road branches off caus: (a) -keluhisa (keluhisize) to cause someone to turn aside; (b) -kelusa (kelusize) to mislead, to guide into error rec. -keluhana (keluhani) to mutually and politely leave the path (speak-ing of two people meeting on the way).
v.i. to be clear or limpid (as water in a pot before it starts boiling): Buewala bu sa kelu-kile mwa piza, the beer is still as clear as water in the pot.
v.i. to look at fixedly and without being seen. rel. -kelyekela (kelyekezi) to look at someone purposely, without being seen
v.t. to extract salt from the ashes of burnt stalks. der. mukele.

v.t. to de-stroy utterly. to exterminate (as people in wars): Silumbu u kelyeng-ile bu–ata mwa ndwa, Silumbu ex- terminated a great many men in his wars rel. -kelyengela (kelyeng- ezi) to destroy in or at (a place). caus. -kelyengisa (kelyengisize) to order or to help someone to de-stroy.
n. action of waiting fig. forgiveness. (from -yema).
v.i. to get very angry. syn. -nyema. caus. -kemukisa (kemukisize) to enrage, to make furious.

v.i. to enter, to go in, to penetrate; to attend: Ni mu boni h'a kena mwa ndu, I saw him enter-ing the house- mwan,a ka u kena sikolo, my child is attending school. spec. exp. Ku kena ka ndwa, to invade; U sike wa ni kena mwa hanu, don't interrupt me (lit: do not get into my mouth). der. make-nelo' mukenelo' sikeniso' sikene-lela. rel. -kenela (kenezi) to enter a place, to enter for a purpose caus. -kenisa (kenisize) or -kenya (ke-nyize) ( l ) to cause someone to ~; to take things inside: Mu kenye li-byana mwa ndu, put the luggage in the house, (2) to involve in: Wena u ka lu Kenya mwa ziezi! you will get us into trouble! rel. -kenyeza (ke-nyelize) (1) to take in for a pur-pose. (2) to order or to help some-one to take things inside int. -ke-nelela (kenelezi) to be determined to U. kenelezi ku uzwa lika za batu, he entered with the determination of stealing people's belongings. rec. -kenelana mwa mandu (kene-lani) to commit adultery with each other's wife

v.l. (1) to be clean, pure (mostly used with past tense): mukeke o kenile, a clean plate; mezi a kenile, pure water. (2) to be holy: Moya o kenile, the Holy Spirit. der. nalikena. caus. -kenisa (kenisize) (1) to make clean, to cleanse: Mu y'o kenisa hande liapalo za mina, go and wash your clothes well. (2) to make holy, to sanctify. (cf.: -twe-tula).

v.t. to disdain, to treat with contempt der. mukendi' mukendwa, lukendende. syn. -nyenya. rel. -kendela (kendezi) to show contempt by giving someone a thing of no value: U ni kendezi sikubo sa kale, he insulted me with a gift of a worn-out blanket caus. -kendisa (kendisize) te keep back food from a guest on the assump- tion that it is unsuitable: Mu sike mwa kendisa mutu lico za canga, do not deprive someone of food which he is accustomed to eat.
v.t. to nag, to con- stantly reproach someone

A: kengama (kengami or kengamile) to lean or lie on one side: Mwanana yo u lata hahulu ku kengama kwa tuko a mahe, this child is fond of Iying near his mother
der. mu-kengami' mukengameni. rel. -keng- amena (kengamezi) to lean or lie by U kengamezi kwa mulilo, he is Iying by the fire.

v.t. to put something near the fire, to roast by the fire (green mealies, etc ) (2) to paddle along the river bank: Mu kengeke mukolo kwa munanga, keep the canoe near the river bank rel. -kengekela (kengekezi) to put green mealies near the fire for someone
v.i. to think, to consider thoughtfully: Ku kengela mwa pi/u, to revolve in the mind der. –engeti.
n. wild creeper producing rubber cf. Iumbongo.
v.t. to wound, to leave scars on someone. der. sike-nyu.
n. Eng. kepi, peaked cap.
v.t. to neg-lect, to do carelessly: Mu sike mwa keshebisa musebezi, don't scamp your work. der. Iikesha.

v.t. (1) to choose, to select, to vote, to take one thing in preference to another: U kettle hembe yende mwa sintolo, he has chosen a nice shirt in the store. (2) to set apart (as the tribute which formerly was brought to the 'li-tunga ! der. muketi' muketisi' Iiketo' liketiso' muketelo' ketululo' buiketo. rel. -ketela (ketezi) (1) to choose for someone: U ni ketele olonji yende, choose a sweet orange for me. (2) to set apart for, to consecrate to: ka ketela Mulimu, to consecrate to God pass, -ke- telwa (ketezwi) to be consecrated to caus. -ketisa (ketisize) (1) to order or to help someone to choose. (2) to make someone pay tribute to the 'Litunga'. stat. rec -ketahana (ketahani or ketahanile) to appear different from others: Likomu za ka pi Anile, za ketahana ka za hao; my cattle are fat, so they are differentiated from yours inv. -ketulula (ketuluzi) to discrimi- nate, to select from others. ref. -iketa (iketile) (1) to be in good health, to be comfortable. (2) to work without haste, leisurely (3) to separate oneself from others, to set oneself apart
n. shell; any shell or part of it used to scrape pots and pans.
adj. five: bate ba ketali-zoho, five people; mafyelo a ketali-zoho, five brooms; linyunywani li (or ze) ketalizoho, five birds.
n. voting. (from: -keta).
n. choice. (from: -keta).
v.i. to be notched, slightly broken at the rim: Pizaya ka i ketu-hile kwa milomo, my clay pot is broken at the rim der. siketu. syn.-monkoka. cf. -shema

v.t. to wonder at, to dread, to regard with terror: Mwan'a ka ba mu ketukile, they wondered at my child. der. muketu. rel. -ketukela (ketukezi) to offend someone by wondering at (a child, etc . . ): U nifoselize ka ka ni ketukela mwan'a ka, he offended me by unduly wondering at my child

v.t. to break slightly; to break asunder. syn.- monkola. fig. to show one's dissat-isfaction by strong words. syn. -longola. rel. -ketulela (ketulezi) to break off for someone: Ketulela munyan'a Tao kwa mwanSa, break off a piece of cassava for your brother fig to speak strongly to someone. caus. -ketulisa (ketulisize) to cause to ~ freq. -ketaula (ke-tauzi) to keep on breaking off, taking off etc . Mu sike mwa ke-taula makonde a sika buzwa, do not keep on taking off raw bananas from the bunch rel. -ketaulela (ke-taulezi) fig. to use strong words when speaking to someone. ref. –i-ketulela (iketukezi) to take for one-self a part of a whole (speaking of many): Mu iketulele mwanSa ni ba ba–wi, share this cassava root with others.
n. discrimination (as applied to race relations) (from: -keta) syn. luketululo.

v.i. to show off (in order to attract attention). der. sikeu. syn. -nyauba. rel. -keubela (keubezi) to show off in order to attract someone's attention: U side wa ni keubela, don't show off to me. caus. -keubisa (keubisize) to make a show (mostly of one's clothes)
v.t. to cast an eye or a glance upon: Zazi la ka mi keukela ka meto mu shwile! the day he casts an eye on you, you will be done for!
v.i. lo sit silently: Ba keyalilefela, ha ba buleli, they are just sitting silently.
v.i. Eng. to write the address on a letter rel. -keya-lela (keyalezi) to ~ for someone sce keyala).
n. Eng. (care of) postal address. (from: -keyala).
expr. used when proposing and answering riddles (lit: there is comes … let it come!)
n. event, occurrence, happening, incident (from:-eza).
n. deed, act, exploit: Kezo yende, a good deed; likezo za Baa-postola, the Acts of the Apostles. (from: -eza).
prep. by (agent): Ni lumilwe ki Mulena, I have been sent by the Li-tunga.
v. particle: it is (used when the predicate is a noun, a pronoun or an adverb): Ki mutu. it is a person; Ki mina, it is you: Ki hande. well done !
n. Eng. key syn. sinotolo.
v.t. to spear a number of people (as in war, or cattle at a funeral): Ba kikitile likomu ze–atafa life la ndat'a bona, they killed a lot of cattle on the death of their father.
v.i. to walk with energy and rapidity. rel. -kilitela (kilitezi) to ~ in a certain direc-tion. caus. -kilitisa (kilitisize) to cause to ~.
adj. thick, stout: mute yomu-kima, a stout person; makonde amakima, thick bananas.

v.t. Eng. to knit der. mukiniti' mukinito' mukinitelo' sikinitiso. rel. -kinitela (kinitezi) to ~ for someone caus. -kinitisa (ki-nitisize) to order or to help to ~. ref. -lkinitela (ikinitezi) to ~ for oneself.
adv. interrog. what is it? why?: Ki–i se mu bata? what are you looking for? Ki–i ha mu bulela swab? why do you say that?
v.t. to stab, to spear. syn: -taba, -kita.
v.i. Sotho. to lie low (land. especially swamps) der. sikisi.

v.t. to stab, to spear: U kitile mute ka lilumo, he stabbed someone with a spear. rel. -kitela (kitezi) to ~ for someone; to stab in or at (a place). caus. -kitisa (kiti-size) to order or to help someone to ~. freq. -kitaka (kitakile) to ~ repeatedly syn. -taba,-kipweka.
v.i. to die sud-denly without any sign of illness rel. -kitibanyeza (kitibanyelize) to kill on someone's behaU caus. -ki-tibanya (kitibanyize) to kill, to stab to death (cattle, etc . . .).
v.i. to run. rel. -ki-timela (kitimezi) to run towards caus. -kitimisa (kitimisize) to cause someone to run. syn. -mata.

v.t. Eng. to lock der. mukii, mukiiluli, kii, sikiiluliso, mukiilulelo. fig. to puzzle: Ni mu kEile. sikusa sa ka si tibile; I bluffed him, for my English is deep rel. -keyela (kiyezi) to lock in or at (a place); to lock for someone caus. -kiisa (kiisize) to cause to lock inv. -kiulula (kiuluzi) to unlock.
